prompt: As a general learning example, why does moving a small set amount into savings automatically on payday usually beat 'saving whatever is left at month-end'?

options.text: Because the transfer happens before everyday spending can absorb the money, removing a monthly willpower decision
Because banks pay extra interest only on payday transfers
Because month-end saving is against most banks' rules
Because the amount automatically grows each month

explanation: 'Whatever is left' is usually close to nothing, because spending expands into available money. Automating the transfer first makes saving the default rather than a leftover.
